cell32_piecewise_compatibility:
#### Work through the two compatibility integrals

The moment expression changes when the cut passes the point load, so **split at its actual position** \(a=L/2\). The value at the single point \(x=a\) does not affect an integral. Here \(E\) and \(I\) are constant and nonzero; only under that restriction can we multiply the zero-rotation and zero-displacement equations by \(-EI\) and cancel the same stiffness factor.

**1. Zero end rotation: integrate the moment diagram.**

$$\begin{aligned}
0&=\int_0^L M(x)\,dx\\
 &=\int_0^a(C_A-R_Ax)\,dx
   +\int_a^L[C_A-R_Ax-P(x-a)]\,dx\\
 &=\left[C_Ax-\frac{R_Ax^2}{2}\right]_0^a
   +\left[C_Ax-\frac{R_Ax^2}{2}-\frac{P(x-a)^2}{2}\right]_a^L\\
 &=\left(C_Aa-\frac{R_Aa^2}{2}\right)
  +\left(C_AL-\frac{R_AL^2}{2}-\frac{P(L-a)^2}{2}
          -C_Aa+\frac{R_Aa^2}{2}\right)\\
 &=\boxed{C_AL-\frac{R_AL^2}{2}-\frac{P(L-a)^2}{2}}.
\end{aligned}$$

The two \(C_Aa\) terms cancel; the two \(R_Aa^2/2\) terms cancel. The point-load term at the lower bound is zero because \((a-a)^2=0\). This integral has units \(\mathrm{N\,mm^2}\); division by \(EI\), whose units are \(\mathrm{N\,mm^2}\), gives rotation.

**2. Zero end displacement: integrate the weighted moment diagram.**

$$\begin{aligned}
0&=\int_0^L(L-x)M(x)\,dx\\
 &=\int_0^a(L-x)(C_A-R_Ax)\,dx
   +\int_a^L(L-x)[C_A-R_Ax-P(x-a)]\,dx.
\end{aligned}$$

The \(C_A-R_Ax\) contribution exists on both intervals. Join those two pieces, but keep the point-load contribution on \([a,L]\) only:

$$\begin{aligned}
0&=C_A\int_0^L(L-x)\,dx
 -R_A\int_0^L(Lx-x^2)\,dx
 -P\int_a^L(L-x)(x-a)\,dx\\
 &=C_A\left[Lx-\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^L
 -R_A\left[\frac{Lx^2}{2}-\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^L
 -P\int_a^L(L-x)(x-a)\,dx.
\end{aligned}$$

For the last integral, use \(u=x-a\). Its bounds become \(u=0\) and \(u=L-a\), while \(L-x=(L-a)-u\):

$$\begin{aligned}
\int_a^L(L-x)(x-a)\,dx
 &=\int_0^{L-a}[(L-a)u-u^2]\,du\\
 &=\left[\frac{(L-a)u^2}{2}-\frac{u^3}{3}\right]_0^{L-a}\\
 &=(L-a)^3\left(\frac12-\frac13\right)
 =\frac{(L-a)^3}{6}.
\end{aligned}$$

Therefore

$$\begin{aligned}
0&=C_A\left(L^2-\frac{L^2}{2}\right)
 -R_A\left(\frac{L^3}{2}-\frac{L^3}{3}\right)
 -\frac{P(L-a)^3}{6}\\
 &=\boxed{\frac{C_AL^2}{2}-\frac{R_AL^3}{6}-\frac{P(L-a)^3}{6}}.
\end{aligned}$$

This integral has units \(\mathrm{N\,mm^3}\); division by \(EI\) gives millimetres. The extra lever arm \(L-x\) makes this a different condition from zero rotation. If \(EI\) varies, retain \(M(x)/(EI(x))\) inside **each** integral; these two constant-stiffness polynomial equations no longer follow.
cell32_numeric_substitution:
#### Check the algebra with numbers

With \(L=450\), \(a=225\) mm and \(P=2\) N, the two equations are

$$450C_A-101250R_A-50625=0,$$
$$101250C_A-15187500R_A-3796875=0.$$

Multiply the first by \(225\) mm, then subtract the second:

$$\begin{aligned}
&(101250-101250)C_A\\
&+(-22781250+15187500)R_A\\
&+(-11390625+3796875)=0,\\
&-7593750R_A-7593750=0.
\end{aligned}$$

Thus \(R_A=-1\) N, and

$$450C_A+101250-50625=0
\quad\Rightarrow\quad C_A=-112.5\ \mathrm{N\,mm}.$$

Substitute into the **integrals**, not just whole-beam equilibrium:

$$\int_0^L M\,dx=-50625+101250-50625=0\ \mathrm{N\,mm^2},$$
$$\int_0^L(L-x)M\,dx=-11390625+15187500-3796875=0\ \mathrm{N\,mm^3}.$$

At the midpoint, only the first moment branch is needed. Integration from the clamped root gives

$$\theta(a)=-\frac{C_Aa-R_Aa^2/2}{EI}=0,$$
$$v(a)=-\frac{C_Aa^2/2-R_Aa^3/6}{EI}
=\frac{949218.75}{3333333.3333}
=0.284765625\ \mathrm{mm}.$$

Both ends are stationary and horizontal; the midpoint is horizontal but displaced downward. These are different geometric statements.
cell41_area_second_moment:
A horizontal strip spans the full constant width \(b\), so \(dA=b\,dz\). The whole rectangle runs from \(z=-h/2\) to \(z=+h/2\):

$$A=\int_{-h/2}^{h/2}b\,dz
=b[z]_{-h/2}^{h/2}
=b\left(\frac h2-\left[-\frac h2\right]\right)=bh=200\ \mathrm{mm^2}.$$

For the second moment, use the same strip and bounds, now weighting every strip by \(z^2\):

$$\begin{aligned}
I_y&=b\int_{-h/2}^{h/2}z^2\,dz
=b\left[\frac{z^3}{3}\right]_{-h/2}^{h/2}\\
&=\frac b3\left[\left(\frac h2\right)^3-\left(-\frac h2\right)^3\right]
=\frac b3\left(\frac{h^3}{8}+\frac{h^3}{8}\right)
=\frac{bh^3}{12}\\
&=20\left[\frac{z^3}{3}\right]_{-5}^{5}
=\frac{20}{3}[125-(-125)]
=1666.6667\ \mathrm{mm^4}.
\end{aligned}$$

The lower half contributes positively too: the integrand is \(z^2\), even where \(z<0\). This is why the two halves add rather than cancel.
cell43_bending_force_and_Q:
#### Integrate the bending stress to recover force and moment

At the cantilever root, \(M=-900\ \mathrm{N\,mm}\), hence \(\sigma_{xx}=900z/I\). For the upper half, \(0\le z\le5\) mm:

$$\begin{aligned}
N_+&=\int_{A_+}\sigma_{xx}\,dA
=\frac{900b}{I}\int_0^5z\,dz
=\frac{900(20)}{1666.6667}\left[\frac{z^2}{2}\right]_0^5\\
&=10.8(12.5)=+135\ \mathrm N.
\end{aligned}$$

For the lower half, keep the signed coordinate:

$$N_-=\frac{900b}{I}\left[\frac{z^2}{2}\right]_{-5}^{0}
=10.8(0-12.5)=-135\ \mathrm N.$$

Thus \(N_++N_-=0\): bending does not create a net axial force. Recovering the signed moment uses a **different** weighting:

$$-\int_A z\sigma_{xx}\,dA
=-\frac{900}{I}\int_Az^2\,dA=-900\ \mathrm{N\,mm}=M.$$

Equivalently, each triangular half-stress resultant acts \(2(5)/3=3.3333\) mm from the neutral axis. The two 135 N resultants form a couple of magnitude \(135(3.3333+3.3333)=900\ \mathrm{N\,mm}\). They are longitudinal forces, not additional applied vertical loads.

#### Integrate the selected area's first moment

For a horizontal cut at coordinate \(z\), select only the rectangle above it. Use \(z'\) as the integration variable so that the fixed lower limit \(z\) is not confused with a running coordinate:

$$\begin{aligned}
Q(z)&=\int_{A^*}z'\,dA=b\int_z^{h/2}z'\,dz'\\
&=b\left[\frac{(z')^2}{2}\right]_z^{h/2}
=\frac b2\left[\left(\frac h2\right)^2-z^2\right].
\end{aligned}$$

At \(z=2.5\) mm:

$$Q=\frac{20}{2}[5^2-2.5^2]
=10(25-6.25)=187.5\ \mathrm{mm^3}.$$

Check without calculus: selected area \(A^*=20(5-2.5)=50\ \mathrm{mm^2}\), centroid \(\bar z^*=(5+2.5)/2=3.75\) mm, so \(A^*\bar z^*=50(3.75)=187.5\ \mathrm{mm^3}\). At the top, the selected area shrinks to zero, so \(Q(5)=0\); at the neutral axis, \(Q(0)=250\ \mathrm{mm^3}\).
cell45_selected_area_force_transfer:
#### Use two neighbouring cuts to see the shear transfer

For a prismatic section and a fixed horizontal cut, \(Q\) and \(I\) do not change with \(x\). Integrating the bending stress over that same selected upper material gives

$$N^*(x)=\int_{A^*}\left[-\frac{M(x)z'}{I}\right]dA
=-\frac{M(x)}{I}\underbrace{\int_{A^*}z'\,dA}_{Q}
=-\frac{M(x)Q}{I}.$$

The force at the next cut is

$$N^*(x+\Delta x)-N^*(x)
=-\frac{Q}{I}[M(x+\Delta x)-M(x)].$$

Since \(M'=V\), division by \(\Delta x\) followed by the small-slice limit gives

$$\frac{dN^*}{dx}=-\frac{VQ}{I}.$$

The upper slice has a left-face force \(-N^*(x)\), a right-face force \(+N^*(x+\Delta x)\), and a longitudinal interface force \(F_{\mathrm{interface}}\). Its balance therefore requires

$$F_{\mathrm{interface}}=N^*(x)-N^*(x+\Delta x)
\approx\frac{VQ}{I}\Delta x.$$

At the chosen \(z=2.5\) mm cut, \(V=2\) N gives \(VQ/I=0.225\ \mathrm{N/mm}\). For example, from \(x=150\) to \(160\) mm, \(M\) changes from \(-600\) to \(-580\ \mathrm{N\,mm}\), while \(N^*\) changes from \(67.50\) to \(65.25\) N. Balance reads

$$-67.50+65.25+2.25=0\ \mathrm N.$$

The interface area is \(b\Delta x\). Dividing its force magnitude by this area cancels \(\Delta x\):

$$|\tau|=\frac{(|V|Q/I)\Delta x}{b\Delta x}
=\frac{|V|Q}{Ib}=0.01125\ \mathrm{MPa}.$$

These steps use a constant cross-section and small-slice beam equilibrium. If the section or selected region varies along \(x\), differentiating \(-MQ/I\) also differentiates the geometry; do not silently reuse the prismatic formula.
cell55_curvature_integrations:
### Integrate curvature using the physical root constraints

For Example A, equilibrium gave \(M(x)=-P(L-x)\). With downward-positive \(v\) and sagging-positive \(M\),

$$-v''=\frac{M}{EI},\qquad v''=-\frac{M}{EI}=\frac{P(L-x)}{EI}.$$

Here \(E\) and \(I\) are constant along the beam. Use \(s\) as the running coordinate in the first integral. The upper bound \(x\) is the station where we want the answer:

$$\begin{aligned}
\theta(x)-\theta(0)
&=\int_0^x v''(s)\,ds
=\frac{P}{EI}\int_0^x(L-s)\,ds\\
&=\frac{P}{EI}\left[Ls-\frac{s^2}{2}\right]_0^x
=\frac{P}{EI}\left(Lx-\frac{x^2}{2}\right).
\end{aligned}$$

The clamp requires \(\theta(0)=0\), so there is no unknown starting rotation. Now integrate the resulting slope, again from the physical root:

$$\begin{aligned}
v(x)-v(0)
&=\int_0^x\theta(s)\,ds
=\frac{P}{EI}\int_0^x\left(Ls-\frac{s^2}{2}\right)ds\\
&=\frac{P}{EI}\left[\frac{Ls^2}{2}-\frac{s^3}{6}\right]_0^x
=\frac{P}{EI}\left(\frac{Lx^2}{2}-\frac{x^3}{6}\right).
\end{aligned}$$

The clamp also requires \(v(0)=0\). In an indefinite-integral approach these same conditions set \(C_1=0\) and \(C_2=0\). Factoring gives

$$\boxed{\theta(x)=\frac{Px(2L-x)}{2EI}},\qquad
\boxed{v(x)=\frac{Px^2(3L-x)}{6EI}}.$$

At \(x=150\) mm, \(EI=(2000)(1666.6667)=3333333.3333\ \mathrm{N\,mm^2}\):

$$\theta(150)=\frac{2}{EI}\left[450(150)-\frac{150^2}{2}\right]
=\frac{112500}{3333333.3333}=0.033750\ \mathrm{rad},$$
$$v(150)=\frac{2}{EI}\left[\frac{450(150)^2}{2}-\frac{150^3}{6}\right]
=\frac{9000000}{3333333.3333}=2.700\ \mathrm{mm}.$$

At the tip, substitute \(x=L\) **before** simplifying:

$$\theta(L)=\frac{P}{EI}\left(L^2-\frac{L^2}{2}\right)=\frac{PL^2}{2EI}=0.060750\ \mathrm{rad},$$
$$v(L)=\frac{P}{EI}\left(\frac{L^3}{2}-\frac{L^3}{6}\right)
=\frac{PL^3}{3EI}=18.225\ \mathrm{mm}.$$

Curvature has units \(1/\mathrm{mm}\); one integration gives a dimensionless slope (reported in radians), and the second gives millimetres. The zero-curvature free tip can have nonzero accumulated slope and displacement. For variable stiffness, use \(-M(s)/(E(s)I(s))\) inside the first integral rather than pulling a constant \(EI\) outside.
cell58_uniform_integrations:
#### Example B: carry out both integrations for the uniform load

The downward load density is \(q=P/L=2/450\ \mathrm{N/mm}\). The cut moment is \(M(x)=-q(L-x)^2/2\), so

$$v''(x)=-\frac{M(x)}{EI}=\frac{q}{2EI}(L-x)^2
=\frac{q}{2EI}(L^2-2Lx+x^2).$$

For constant \(EI\), integrate from the clamp and apply \(\theta(0)=0\):

$$\begin{aligned}
\theta(x)&=\frac{q}{2EI}\int_0^x(L^2-2Ls+s^2)\,ds\\
&=\frac{q}{2EI}\left[L^2s-Ls^2+\frac{s^3}{3}\right]_0^x\\
&=\frac{q}{2EI}\left(L^2x-Lx^2+\frac{x^3}{3}\right).
\end{aligned}$$

Integrate once more and apply \(v(0)=0\):

$$\begin{aligned}
v(x)&=\frac{q}{2EI}\int_0^x\left(L^2s-Ls^2+\frac{s^3}{3}\right)ds\\
&=\frac{q}{2EI}\left[\frac{L^2s^2}{2}-\frac{Ls^3}{3}+\frac{s^4}{12}\right]_0^x\\
&=\frac{qx^2}{24EI}(6L^2-4Lx+x^2).
\end{aligned}$$

At the tip the powers of \(L\) combine, but the fractions must still be added:

$$\theta(L)=\frac{qL^3}{2EI}\left(1-1+\frac13\right)
=\frac{qL^3}{6EI}=0.020250\ \mathrm{rad},$$
$$v(L)=\frac{qL^4}{2EI}\left(\frac12-\frac13+\frac1{12}\right)
=\frac{qL^4}{2EI}\left(\frac14\right)
=\frac{qL^4}{8EI}=6.834375\ \mathrm{mm}.$$

At \(x=150\) mm the intermediate checks are \(v''=0.000060\ \mathrm{mm^{-1}}\), \(\theta=0.014250\) rad, and \(v=1.209375\) mm. The same total 2 N load spread over the span does not generate the same \(M(x)\), curvature, or displacement as a 2 N tip force. Both examples satisfy the same two root constraints, but integrate different curvature fields.
